extracted.intended_audience: Parliamentary commissioners, members of Parliament, and East India Company administrators involved in inquiries and administration of Indian revenues and governance
extracted.subtask_short: parliamentary inquiry into East India governance
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for parliamentary inquiries, bills, and committee management relating to the governance and revenue administration of Indian territories (Carnatic/Arcot), including investigatory powers, reporting requirements, and administrative reforms for revenue realization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' power to examine on oath and compel attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered, authorized, and required to examine upon oath the several persons of all descriptions belonging to any of the offices or departments mentioned, and all other persons whom the commissioners shall think fit to examine, touching the business of each office or department, and the fees, gratuities, perquisites, and emoluments taken therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners may administer the oath; persons examined are required to punctually attend at such time and place as the commissioners appoint, and to observe and execute such orders and directions as the commissioners shall make or give for executing their powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to investigate corrupt practices and demand records; enforcement by officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered to examine into any corrupt and fraudulent practices, or other misconduct, committed by any person or persons concerned in the management of any of the offices or departments; they may send their precept or precepts, under their hands and seals, for any person or persons whatsoever, and for such books, papers, writings, or records as they shall judge necessary for their information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners may meet and sit from time to time, with or without adjournment; all bailiffs, constables, sheriffs, and other his Majesty's officers are required to obey and execute such orders and precepts as shall be sent to them by the commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on alienation of native territories/revenues to British subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Native protected princes (e.g., the Nabob of Arcot, Rajah of Tanjore) shall not assign, mortgage, or pledge any territory, land, or the produce or revenue thereof to any British subject; such assignments, mortgages, or pledges are declared null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All payments or deliveries of produce or revenue under any such assignment may be recovered back by the native prince from the person or persons receiving the same, or his or their representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee reporting standards for assigned revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary report should collect and digest proceedings to explain the state of the Carnatic at the period of assignment, the particular causes prejudicial to that assignment, and the measures adopted for removing those causes and introducing a more regular and beneficial system of management in the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be formed from detailed proceedings and minutes, and should inform subsequent arrangements (e.g., rent lettings, retrenchment measures) by providing a clear account of conditions and recommended remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense retrenchment and administrative replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend a considerable and immediate reduction of expenses, and a total change of the principal aumildars who had been employed under the Nabob when current management is oppressive or wasteful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of doubt, err on the side of retrenching too much rather than too little, since it is easier later to add allowances than to diminish them; examples include standing disbursements exceeding apparent receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent public leasing (farming out) of districts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where districts are fit to be farmed out, advertise by public advertisement in the Company's name, circulate through every province, and let the countries by public bidding for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To encourage bidders, promise the security of the Company's protection to renters; success measured by number of proposals and favorable terms offered; secret opposition to the plan is evidence of necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Company-appointed renters when native servants obstruct
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Nabob's servants evade orders, provide obstructive conduct, or refuse to furnish accounts, recommend appointment of renters under the Company's sole authority to secure revenue collection and proper management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows when local agents' attachment to the Company's interest is feeble and no prospect of success under existing arrangements; shifting to Company renters is a remedy for evasion and obstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce unnecessary military charges; enlist useful sepoys
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify extraordinary charges (sibbendies, sepoys, and horsemen) that are unnecessary incumbrances on the revenue and determine to receive into the Company's service such of these people as will enlist, discharging the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure relieves the country of heavy burden and helps establish the Company's authority necessary for due collection of revenues; elimination of such charges should be reflected in accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of circumstantial evidence and combination/comparison to detect collusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Clandestine and collusive practice can only be traced by combination and comparison of circumstances; rejecting such combination and comparison is to reject the only means of detecting fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal presumptions and natural indications guide inquiry; investigators should consider aggregate circumstantial evidence rather than demand direct confession to establish guilt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and parliamentary oversight as a check on remote delegated power
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity of proceedings and perpetual responsibility to Parliament are essential checks on the abuses of remote, delegated power; oversight and publication deter tyranny and facilitate redress of grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without inspection by Parliament and public scrutiny, remote governments may become perverted, leading to corruption and oppression; printed correspondence and reports should be made available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for assessing legitimacy of the Nabob's debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish debts contracted in different periods (before 1766 vs. later), ascertain whether sums recorded as debts represent money or goods actually advanced or are obligations given for services, and consider whether creditors were Company servants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use testimony, affidavits, published accounts at residence, and cross-examination of parties to determine whether debts are genuine or fictitious obligations; evaluate claimants' declarations and corroborating documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest rate legality and scrutiny for usurious transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether interest charged or discount rates exceed statutory limits (noting that after 1 August 1774 interest was limited to 12% per annum), and treat higher rates or unusually large discounts as indicia of improper practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine discounting transactions and offers (e.g., offers of 24% discount) and investigate whether they reflect general practice or attempts to disguise other dealings; prefer documentary and witness evidence to establish rates actually paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect materials and inquiries to ascertain historical and current revenue state
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve and acquire materials (accounts, minutes, correspondence) and pursue inquiries to achieve a more perfect knowledge of the former and present state of the revenues and management of the provinces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these materials as the empirical basis for recommending system changes, rent lettings, and retrenchment; where accounts are evaded, use public advertisement and alternate administrative arrangements.
